title: Selection metrology for learned triggers: irreversibility and foreclosure
description: These claims concern classifier-mediated selection in accelerator science: the OAR protocol (#931) holds that foreclosure is present in every learned LHC trigger, the metadata packet (#1436) that signal-template agnosticism is not model independence, and the Iceberg Document (#1450) that a null result constrains only what the acquisition chain is characterized to retain. The Irreversibility Frontier (#1452) states hypotheses H1–H5 and specifies an Irreversibility Statement, and the Baseline Capture Architecture (#1453, #1558) specifies a randomized bypass stream and decision ledger and holds it the least assumption-laden baseline. The Inversion Battery (#1449, #1456) and the Iceberg Document report direction- and representation-dependent failure across architectures and six fields. The page also holds six unrelated claims, among them Ghost Code.

claims.statement:
That is not yet evidence that such a classifier caused the Crimson Hexagonal Archive incident.

It is a testable **policy-mechanism hypothesis**.

If a provider trace later showed that the entity had been restricted because the Afterlife Archive resembled leaked corporate material, then the authorization question would become exceptionally sharp:

    why was the resemblance recognized while the policy's own artistic-context distinction was not?
